baroque.name: Baroque
baroque.summary: Music built from interweaving lines (counterpoint) over a constantly moving bass, with ornamented melodies and steady, motor-like rhythm.
traits: Counterpoint: several independent melodic lines at once
Basso continuo: a bass line plus harpsichord filling in the chords
Terraced dynamics: whole sections loud or soft, rarely gradual
Ornaments: trills, mordents and decorated long notes
One steady pulse and mood per movement
baroque.instruments: Strings, harpsichord, organ, recorder/flute, oboe, bassoon, natural trumpet, timpani

classical.name: Classical
classical.summary: Clear, balanced phrases with a singable tune on top and light, transparent accompaniment, where every phrase ends in a satisfying cadence.
traits: Homophony: one main melody with accompaniment beneath
Crescendos and contrasts of mood within a movement
The string quartet and the symphony orchestra take their classic shape
classical.instruments: String quartet, fortepiano, flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, horns, trumpets, timpani

romantic.name: Romantic
romantic.summary: Emotion first: long singing melodies, rich and colourful harmony, flexible tempo (rubato), big dynamic swells and larger orchestras.
traits: Rubato: tempo breathes, slowing at phrase ends
Wide piano arpeggios held by the sustain pedal
Richer chords: borrowed chords, diminished sevenths, chromatic colour
Huge dynamic range, from whisper to full orchestra
romantic.instruments: Grand piano, full string sections, clarinets, horns, harp, expanded brass and percussion

composers.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
composers.bio: The great master of counterpoint: several melodies woven together over a walking bass, every line meaningful.

composers.name: Antonio Vivaldi
works: Concerto for Two Violins in A minor
composers.bio: The 'Red Priest' of Venice: energetic string concertos built on driving repeated-note basses and catchy, repeating patterns.

composers.name: George Frideric Handel
composers.bio: Grand, ceremonial music for London audiences: broad harmonies, trumpets and timpani, and big choruses everyone could follow.

composers.name: Joseph Haydn
composers.bio: 'Father of the string quartet and the symphony': witty, cheerful, perfectly balanced phrases with the odd surprise.

composers.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
composers.bio: Effortless, song-like melodies over light Alberti-bass accompaniment, with graceful appoggiaturas and flawless proportions.

composers.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
composers.bio: The bridge to Romanticism: dramatic contrasts, explosive dynamics, driving rhythm and a struggle-to-triumph arc.

composers.name: Franz Schubert
composers.bio: Master of the art song (Lied): a voice-like melody with an expressive piano accompaniment that paints the mood.

composers.name: Felix Mendelssohn
composers.bio: Light, quicksilver Romanticism: sparkling fast strings, clear forms, elegant lyricism.

composers.name: Frédéric Chopin
composers.bio: The poet of the piano: singing nocturne melodies with ornamental turns over wide, pedalled left-hand arpeggios, and a constantly breathing rubato.

composers.name: Franz Liszt
composers.bio: The first superstar pianist: thundering, virtuosic textures, cascading arpeggios and huge dynamic climaxes.

composers.name: Johannes Brahms
composers.bio: Romantic warmth with Baroque craft: rich, autumnal textures, inner counter-melodies and the dark glow of clarinet and viola.

composers.name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
composers.bio: Big-hearted melody and orchestral colour: soaring tunes over pulsing strings, horns, harp and climaxes that sweep everything up.

piano.name: Solo keyboard
piano.summary: One player. Harpsichord for Baroque styles, piano for Classical and Romantic.

parts.melody: Right hand plays the tune (plus chord tones beneath it in loud passages)
parts.keys_lh: Left hand plays the bass and the accompaniment figure (walking bass, Alberti bass or wide pedalled arpeggios)

piano.why: the most intimate setting: one instrument carries both melody and harmony, which keeps the tune very clear

string_quartet.name: String quartet
string_quartet.summary: Two violins, viola and cello. The Classical era's favourite chamber group.

parts.melody: First violin sings the vocal line
parts.inner_hi: Second violin fills in harmony or plays a counter-line
parts.inner_lo: Viola holds the middle of the chord

string_quartet.why: four equal voices give clean voice-leading and a warm, blended, unmistakably classical sound

chamber.name: Chamber ensemble
chamber.summary: A wind soloist with strings (and keyboard): flute for Baroque and Classical styles, clarinet for Romantic ones.

parts.melody: A wind soloist (flute or clarinet) carries the tune

chamber.why: a contrasting wind colour on the melody makes the tune stand out from the strings

orchestra.name: Orchestra
orchestra.summary: String sections plus woodwinds, horns or trumpets, timpani (and harp in Romantic style).

parts.melody: Violin section on the tune, doubled by flute or oboe in loud sections
parts.bass: Cellos / double basses / bassoon on the bass line
parts.winds: Oboes, clarinets, bassoons sustain harmony in louder sections
parts.timpani: Timpani mark cadences in the loudest sections

orchestra.why: the full colour palette: the song's loud choruses can swell into the whole orchestra
